independent.summary: The PATCH no-op shortcut `if (member.role === role) return res.json({userId, role})` is still a read-derived branch in front of the write — exactly the shape KOL-141 set out to remove. A request that read the member as `owner` and asks for `owner`, racing a concurrent demotion to `editor`, returns 200 `{role:'owner'}` without writing anything, so the client is told a promotion succeeded while the member is an editor. No invariant is breached (nothing is written), but the answer is a lie taken from a stale read.

The updated falsification note is wrong about the new filter: "drop the `$ne` on `$$o.userId` from `notTheLastOwner` and the first write stops matching" no longer holds. Without that `$ne` the expression reduces to `$size(owners) >= 1 || $size(owners) == 0`, which is unconditionally true, so that mutant makes *every* write match and the floor never holds at all — the opposite of what the note tells a reader to expect, which defeats the file's stated purpose of naming the mutants its cases kill.

triageGrades.reason: The change is entirely inside the owner/editor/viewer role-assignment and member-removal endpoints and alters the invariant that keeps a workspace holding an owner — role and privilege management is authorization, so this category is touched.
No credentials, tokens, env vars or hashing logic appear anywhere in the diff.
No billing, pricing or seat-charging code is involved; the spec explicitly leaves seat billing out of scope.

Right that it is touched — `DELETE /workspace/members/:userId` now carries the floor unconditionally, changing when a membership is actually pulled (the cited line 341 is off by ~120 lines, but the category call is correct).
Only local MongoDB writes and in-process Express routes; no outbound calls or third-party integrations.
No version bumps, migrations, deploy config or dependency changes — just route/lib code, tests and prose docs.

summary: The local model reported nothing on a change that is substantively correct, so it missed only two low-severity leftovers (the stale-read no-op shortcut and a now-false falsification note), and its triage was right except for calling auth untouched on a change that is entirely about role and privilege management.
